responses: AI (Artificial Intelligence) is the simulation of human intelligence by machines — enabling them to learn, reason, and make decisions.
Artificial Intelligence refers to computer systems engineered to perform tasks typically requiring human perception, reasoning, and learning.
intents.follow_up: AI encompasses subfields like Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Computer Vision, and NLP.

responses: Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI where systems automatically learn patterns from data without being explicitly programmed for every scenario.
ML uses statistical algorithms to train models on historical data to predict outcomes or classify new inputs accurately.
intents.follow_up: ML includes Supervised Learning (e.g. KNN, SVM), Unsupervised Learning (e.g. Clustering), and Reinforcement Learning.

responses: LLMs (Large Language Models) are massive deep neural networks trained on vast textual datasets. They predict token sequences to generate natural language.
Large Language Models use the Transformer architecture with self-attention to understand, generate, and reason over text.
intents.follow_up: Modern LLMs like Llama 3, GPT-4, and Claude power interactive conversational AI and code generation.

responses: Deep Learning uses multi-layered artificial neural networks (ANNs) to model high-level abstractions in data like images, audio, and text.
Deep Learning is a subset of ML based on deep architectures: CNNs for vision, Transformers for sequences, and RNNs for temporal data.
intents.follow_up: Deep learning requires substantial compute (GPUs) and large datasets for training.

responses: NLP (Natural Language Processing) enables computers to read, analyze, interpret, and generate human languages using linguistic and statistical methods.
intents.follow_up: Common NLP tasks include tokenization, TF-IDF vectorization, named entity recognition, and sentiment analysis.
